title: Splay traversal conjecture
formal: Is there an absolute C such that accessing the preorder of any n-key binary search tree by standard bottom-up Splay, starting from any other tree on those keys, costs at most Cn?
definitions: The keys are {1,…,n}, n≥1, and each tree has one node per key, with every left-subtree key smaller and every right-subtree key larger than its root. The access sequence is the preorder of a fixed target tree: visit its root, then recursively its left and right subtrees. Start from an arbitrary initial search tree. To access x, follow ordinary search from the root and then repeatedly rotate x upward: if its parent is the root, rotate x above its parent (zig); if x and its parent are both left children or both right children, first rotate the parent above its parent and then x above its parent (zig-zig); otherwise rotate x above its parent and then above its new parent (zig-zag). A rotation preserves the in-order key order and moves the intervening subtree to the vacated child link. Stop when x is root. Charge one unit per node visited by the search and one per rotation. No insertions, deletions, preprocessing rotations or lookahead modification are allowed. The bound quantifies over both trees and all n.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of this linear bound or a family whose cost divided by n is unbounded. Proving the property for a different BST algorithm does not suffice.
context: The pattern-avoidance work studies preorder-like access structures and distinguishes the traversal conjecture for Splay from results for other BST algorithms.
why: The traversal conjecture is a classical structured-access barrier within the broader dynamic-optimality program.

import_provenance.original_title: The traversal conjecture for splay trees
import_provenance.original_statement: Starting from any n-key BST, does splaying the keys in the preorder sequence of any other BST on the same keys take O(n) total time? Mehlhorn and coauthors study this fundamental special case through pattern avoidance and obtain relaxations for Greedy.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The statement is specifically about Splay; linear-time results for variants of Greedy with preprocessing do not prove it.

sentences: The requested keys are the preorder of a fixed target search tree.
The initial search tree may be unrelated to that target.
Each access uses the ordinary bottom-up Splay rotations.
Search visits and rotations are both charged.
The assertion is a universal linear total bound for the complete traversal.
